disease_label_per_paper: Enteroviral meningitis in an immunocompetent adult man with atypical afebrile presentation
presentation_summary: 40-year-old man with hypertension presented with gradual severe headache, neck pain radiating to the scalp, mild nausea, and transient blurry vision.
He denied fever, chills, sudden thunderclap onset, prior migraine history, loss of consciousness, dizziness, vomiting, diarrhea, travel, or animal exposure.
Exam showed normal mental status, normal neurologic examination, bilateral paraspinal tenderness, and no nuchal rigidity or classic meningeal signs.
Initial blood pressure was elevated at 148/103 mmHg; CBC showed mild leukocytosis with neutrophilic predominance.
Lumbar puncture showed mildly elevated opening pressure, clear CSF, very mild pleocytosis, elevated protein, normal glucose, and low RBC count without xanthochromia.
CT brain/cervical spine and MRI/MRA brain/neck were unremarkable.

A CSF meningitis-encephalitis PCR panel detected enterovirus and was negative for bacterial pathogens, HSV-1/2, VZV, CMV, HHV-6, parechovirus, and Cryptococcus; a separate enterovirus PCR was negative.
Empiric ceftriaxone, vancomycin, acyclovir, and dexamethasone were stopped after enterovirus interpretation; symptoms resolved with supportive care and he was discharged on hospital day 3.

quality_warnings: Enterovirus PCR result is kept in microbiology/confirmatory sections with use_in_ranking=false for presentation-focused ranking.
Afebrile presentation and absent nuchal rigidity are retained as negative structured observations rather than omitted.
Mild transaminitis is structured because it was reported, but it is nonspecific for the viral meningitis manifold.
